task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the length of the longest sublists.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method LongestSublistLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (length: nat)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The returned length is the length of the longest sublist within the input sequence of sequences
    - The length is at least zero
    - For each sublist in the input, if its length equals the returned length, then it is among the longest sublists
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method LongestSublistLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (maxLength: int)

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The input is a sequence of sequences (sublists), possibly empty
Dafny specification:
    // No specific preconditions needed, as the input can be any sequence of sequences

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The returned value is the length of the longest sublist among the input sequences

Dafny specification:
    ensures maxLength >= 0
    ensures forall sub :: sub in lists ==> |sub| <= maxLength

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method LongestSublistLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (maxLength: int)
    ensures maxLength >= 0
    ensures forall sub :: sub in lists ==> |sub| <= maxLength
{
    maxLength := 0;
    var i := 0;
    while i < |lists|
        invariant 0 <= i <= |lists|
        invariant maxLength >= 0
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> |lists[j]| <= maxLength
    {
        if |lists[i]| > maxLength {
            maxLength := |lists[i]|;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```
